## Why Git? {.center}

(or any other version control software)

## Situation #1: Review of a draft document (offline mode)

::: {.incremental}
- Difficult to know which copy of the document contains which change.
- Duplication of the same information many times, occupying space on your hard drive.
:::

## Situation #2: A group coding project

::: {.row}
::: {.labelled}
::: {.pill .pill-lg .p-orange}
Alice
:::

Project copy #1
:::

::: {.labelled}
::: {.pill .pill-lg .p-tan}
Laura
:::

Project copy #2
:::

::: {.labelled}
::: {.pill .pill-lg .p-salmon}
John
:::

Project copy #3
:::
:::

. . .

::: {.focus}
**Challenge:** How to merge all these different copies together and maintain a final copy of the project?
:::

. . .

::: {.box}
John makes his changes and sends his project to Laura
:::

. . .

::: {.box}
Laura merges her changes and sends it to Alice
:::

. . .

::: {.box}
Alice merges her changes, reviews and maintains the final copy
:::

## Situation #2: Consequences of this solution

::: {.incremental}
- Manual approach
- Time consuming
- Error prone
- Not scalable
- Inefficient
:::

. . .

::: {.focus}
Thus, we need an efficient system that tracks different versions of a project and allows the team to know **who** has made changes to the project, **when** and **why**!
:::

## What is Git?

Mentimeter: <https://www.menti.com/alx2mugaqr1n>

## What is Git? {.center}

Menti Poll

## What is Git?

- Git is the most used version control system. More than 90% of software projects around the world use Git.
- It was created in 2005 by Linus Torvalds, the same creator of the Linux OS.
- It is free, open source, fast and scalable.
- It is a version control software meant to keep track of the entire history of a project and allows collaboration of any size.
- Git + GitHub (GitLab) allows distributed / de-centralized collaboration within the team of collaborators.

## How to use Git? {.center}

The workshop of today!

::: {.checks}
